plan_created_event.rationale: Scope "complex" in domain "software-engineering" with 4 capability needs. Planned 4 specialist role(s): Software Engineer [code-execution], Documentation Writer [document-authoring], Generalist Worker [data-analysis], Verification Engineer [browser-verification]. Mission Coordinator added because 3+ specialists require integration.

specialists_run_order: SEQUENTIAL (for...of loop in orchestrator.ts line 554, awaited one at a time)
specialists_run_order_evidence: software-engineer-1 finished at seq 25 → documentation-writer-2 started at seq 26 → documentation-writer-2 finished at seq 32 → generalist-worker-3 started at seq 33 → generalist-worker-3 failed at seq 37 → verification event at seq 38 → mission-finished at seq 39.

coordination_graph.key_observation: documentation-writer-2's only upstream edge is FROM the coordinator. When the coordinator didn't run (mission aborted due to timeout before reaching the coordinator step), documentation-writer-2 had NO upstream inputs.

brief_sent_to_documentation_writer_2.structure: Mission: <full outcome>; Your assignment in it: Documents the change and its usage.; Mission context: <full context>; Hard constraints: <constraints array joined>; Success criteria: <domain-inherent criteria>; Your workspace may already hold the mission's repository checkout; otherwise it starts empty...; Deliverables go to your own workspace. Finish with your artifact paths when done.
brief_sent_to_documentation_writer_2.critical_omission: The brief did NOT include 'Inputs from colleagues' because upstream.length === 0 (no upstream edges fired). The brief did NOT say 'Other workers will produce the code; you should ONLY produce README.md'. The worker saw the full mission outcome (which lists all 7 capabilities including 'create a service request', 'list requests', 'update status', 'persist records', 'reject invalid inputs', 'include automated tests', 'include a README') and reasonably interpreted its assignment ('Documents the change and its usage') as: 'I need to document a working application. To document it, the application must exist. No upstream inputs are available. I'll produce the whole thing myself.'

root_cause_analysis.primary_defect: BRIEF DEFECT — the brief tells each worker the FULL mission outcome, then says 'Your assignment: <responsibility>'. Without explicit role-scoping ('produce ONLY README.md; the code will come from another worker'), and without visible upstream inputs (because the coordinator didn't run), the worker reasonably produces the whole app.
root_cause_analysis.secondary_defect: COORDINATION GRAPH DEFECT — the writer's only upstream edge is via the coordinator. The planner's buildEdges function (src/organization/organization-planner.ts) puts all workers downstream of the coordinator (coordinator → writer handoff). When the coordinator is skipped (timeout or aborted), the writer has no direct upstream edge from the code-worker.
root_cause_analysis.tertiary_defect: GOAL COMPILER OVER-EXTRACTION (FROZEN) — the goal compiler extracted 4 capability needs (code-execution, document-authoring, data-analysis, browser-verification) for what's essentially a code-execution-only mission (CLI app with tests). The 'document-authoring' capability need triggered a separate Documentation Writer specialist; the 'data-analysis' need triggered a Generalist Worker; the 'browser-verification' need triggered a Verification Engineer. None of these were necessary for the actual mission.

proposed_correction.scope: TARGETED — modify only the planner's buildEdges function (NON-FROZEN, src/organization/organization-planner.ts).
proposed_correction.change: Add a DIRECT handoff edge from each non-coordinator worker to the writer, EVEN when a coordinator is present. The coordinator's role is preserved (still receives reports, still integrates); the writer just gains a parallel direct upstream edge from each code-worker.
proposed_correction.rationale: When the coordinator doesn't run (timeout/cancelled), the writer still sees upstream worker artifacts directly. The brief's 'Inputs from colleagues' section would fire, listing the code-worker's files. The writer would then know: 'The code-worker has produced X, Y, Z. I should focus on documentation.'
proposed_correction.implementation_status: PROPOSED ONLY — G7-19F brief says 'Only propose a targeted correction if the evidence proves a coordination defect.' The evidence proves the defect. The correction is documented here for the next mission to implement. Implementing it in G7-19F would be out of scope (G7-19F is about acceptance contract integrity, not worker coordination behavior changes that need their own test coverage).
